question.prompt: A line segment parallel to the vertical axis in the original figure has length 3 in the pictorial drawing. What was its original length?

solutions.explanation:
Assuming the recorded unscaled oblique-dimetric convention for a horizontally placed plane figure, with “vertical axis” meaning its original planar \(y\)-axis, the drawn length is half the original length. Reversing this rule gives the original length \(2\times3=6\).

The displayed question does not specify the drawing convention. If this direction were drawn at full length, the original length would instead be \(3\), so \(6\) is conditional. The cited source heading is not supplied here, and the recorded provisional reconciliation still requires root inspection before grading publication.
solutions.title: Reverse the qualified half-length rule
